quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, what should you use to show you are turning?

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: Use hand signals when your turn signals do not work. This tells other drivers which direction you plan to turn.

questions.question: What does a green arrow and a red light together mean?

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.
Vehicles moving in any direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow points, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?

options.text: Rectangle.
Square.
Circle.
Octagon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon.
questions.explanation: Stop signs are eight-sided. All eight-sided signs tell drivers to stop completely before moving forward.

questions.question: In Alaska, when must you wear a seat belt?

options.text: Only for children under 16.
Only in the front seat.
Everyone in a moving vehicle at all times.
Only when driving faster than 50 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in a moving vehicle at all times.
questions.explanation: Everyone must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle. The driver is responsible for making sure all passengers under 16 wear their seat belts.

questions.question: Why should you use extra caution near a pedestrian with a white cane?

options.text: He or she is deaf.
He or she is a police officer.
He or she is blind.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means the person is blind. Slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Before stopping, check your mirrors and blind spots.
Slow down by releasing the gas before using the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: All three methods help prevent rear-end collisions. Avoid sudden stops, check mirrors before stopping, and slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal before braking.

questions.question: What does this sign tell drivers?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
An intersection is coming.
Road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the right lane on a multilane road ends. Traffic in the right lane must move to the left.

questions.question: You are approaching a flashing red traffic light. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Proceed only when it is safe to do so.
Treat it like a stop sign.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Stop completely, look both ways for traffic and pedestrians, then go only when it is safe.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake hard. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Release the gas pedal to slow down gradually. Once moving very slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull to a safe area.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes on a multilane road?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert drivers behind you.
Slow down to shrink your blind spot.
Look in mirrors, then stare straight ahead.
None of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of these.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. This is the safe way to change lanes.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: Octagonal signs are always stop signs. Stop completely when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line down the middle. What does this tell you?

options.text: You are on a two-way road.
You are on a one-way road.
The road is under repair.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a two-way road.
questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines can be crossed to pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving on a two-lane road without bike lanes and see a cyclist ahead going the same direction. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the cyclist.
Keep driving straight. The cyclist must get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to alert the cyclist that you are about to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the cyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist like you would pass any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet between your mirror and the cyclist, or 5 feet on faster roads or with multiple cyclists. Do not honk—it may startle the rider and cause a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Lane shifting.
Low clearance.
Added lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: When driving across railroad tracks with no signals or gates, what should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Check that you have enough room to cross the tracks completely before entering. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle that just parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Assume the driver will open the door as you approach.
Speed up.
Slam on your brakes.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver will open the door as you approach.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked vehicle, assume the driver may open the door. Drive with caution near parked cars.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines on the road mean:

options.text: Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during daylight only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Sit in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Sound your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, turn on your hazard flashers. Exit the roadway carefully and park where other drivers can see you easily. Lift your hood to signal that your vehicle is disabled.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive the speed limit with caution.
Never drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or sleet appears. These conditions make roads slippery. Driving slower than the speed limit may be necessary for safety.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between traffic mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass even if it could be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means vehicles in both directions can pass. Only pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.
